transcript:
APPROVED ON OCTOBER 21, 2026

# REGULAR MEETING OF THE SOUTH BURLINGTON SCHOOL BOARD

Wednesday, October 7, 2026

Regular Session at 6:00 p.m.

South Burlington School District Administrative Office

577 Dorset Street, South Burlington, VT

## Call Regular meeting to order

Seamus Abshere called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. (no Executive Session).

## REGULAR MEETING

### Present

Seamus Abshere, Jennifer Lawrence, Dan Boyer, Michelle Boyer, Elissa Galvez, Emilee Hoffman, Tom Chittenden, Oliver Kunz, Charu Magar

### Administration/Staff

Dr. Joe Clark, Jean-Marie Clark, Suzanne Gruendling, Olivia Kane, Lissa McDonald, Sarah Pineda, Kat Yun, Beth Adreon

### Guests

Gerry Silverstein, Veronica Negruta

### Call to Order

Chair Seamus Abshere called the regular meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. He noted that the Executive Session had been canceled because there were no topics of discussion. The Pledge of Allegiance was said.

## ANNOUNCEMENTS AND AMENDMENTS TO THE AGENDA

### Announcements

Michelle Boyer mentioned that the Vermont School Board Association Annual Conference would be October 29-30 and wondered about registration. Joe Clark offered to look into it. Seamus Abshere announced that on October 20, the first Act 170 Merger Committee would meet, facilitated by Craig Ahrens-Martin.

### Amendment to Agenda

It was agreed by the Board to amend the agenda and to not review the Monthly 2.4 Financial Condition and Activities Review or 2.3 Treatment of Community, as warned, and to move those items to the next scheduled meeting on October 21.

## Comments and Questions

Public comment was received from Gerry Silverstein regarding the January 14, 2026 presentation on Center for Technology Essex by Meghan Sweet and Principal John Burke. He felt that it presented data in a misleading and incomplete way. He contended that comparing acceptance rates without examining applicants' qualifications, drawing conclusions from very small sample sizes, and highlighting the HVAC program's zero acceptances among four South Burlington applicants created a distorted picture of potential bias. Gerry Silverstein also challenged the portrayal of rejection as a life-changing event and argued that math and science are essential to careers such as HVAC, plumbing, and carpentry. Overall, Gerry Silverstein urged school officials to present data more responsibly, avoid drawing unsupported conclusions, and to provide students with accurate information about educational and career pathways.

Public comment was also received from Veronica Negruta, a resident as well as an employee of the school district, who expressed concern that increased school taxes are not being used wisely, particularly when it comes to staffing and employee compensation. She questioned why district employees are paid less than third-party hires and workers in neighboring districts. She urged the district to reconsider its staffing and budgeting practices and to demonstrate greater appreciation for the employees who support its students.

Public comment was also received from Sarah Pineda. She suggested that the Board revise the policy language from "maintain wellness" to "apply health literacy skills to make informed decisions about physical, mental, and social well-being". She argued that the revised wording emphasizes skills students can learn and demonstrate, rather than suggesting wellness is entirely within their control. Sarah Pineda also stressed that health literacy should be valued equally with financial literacy in the school curriculum.

## Focus on Student Learning

Oliver Kunz shared that the SBX team has been organizing career exploration opportunities, including a health sciences showcase, hospital shadowing, informational interviews with professionals, and a career event attended by 209 SBHS students. Students also learned about career opportunities in electrical aviation, engineering, advanced manufacturing, technology, and business.

Charu Magar shared that kindergarten students were invited and attended a SeaWolves football game on October 2 to celebrate the Class of 2039. A high school pep rally was held to build excitement and school spirit ahead of the Homecoming football game. She explained how Chamberlin students were scheduled to participate in a whole-school movement and music performance at the high school on October 8, from 6-8 p.m. Charu Magar also announced that on October 12, senior SLAM leaders and freshman advisory groups would volunteer at local nonprofits, including elementary schools, followed by the SLAM Olympics organized by aspiring junior SLAM leaders.

Oliver Kunz noted that parent-teacher conferences were scheduled for October 22 and 23.

There were no questions.

## DISCUSSION ITEMS

### Monthly 2.4 Financial Condition and Activities Review

Seamus Abshere noted that this had been removed from the agenda.

### Policy F4 Investigation and Response to Harassment, Hazing, and Bullying of Students *(First Reading)*

Joe Clark noted that some changes had been made and how the Board would be required to adopt the model policy for the December 15 implementation. He planned to put a redline version of the document together for the next meeting to clearly show the specific changes. There were no questions.

### Policy D9 Electronic Communications Between Employees and Students *(First Reading)*

Joe Clark noted that, as with the other policy, he planned to put a redline version of the document together for the next meeting to clearly show the changes that had been made. There were no questions.

## ACTION ITEMS

### Ends Policy Update *(Third Reading)*

Seamus Abshere introduced the suggested final version of the Ends Policy and reminded the Board that it was a living document. The Board discussed revising the "maintain wellness" section to better emphasize students' ability to develop and apply health literacy skills. Board members generally supported clarifying the wording to align with other policy statements, such as financial literacy, while keeping it concise and emphasizing age-appropriate understanding of physical and mental health. Board members expressed some uncertainty about the exact wording of the financial and health literacy sections but agreed it was important to move forward rather than spend excessive time refining the language. They emphasized creating a clear, concise document that reflects stakeholder input and one that could be revised as needed. The updated language will be tested through upcoming monitoring, allowing the Board to identify any confusion or areas that need improvement.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to adopt the new Ends Policy as provided in the Board packet with the edits made during the meeting. Dan Boyer moved; Tom Chittenden seconded the motion. All were in favor; the motion passed.

### Act 170 Merger Committee - Third Board Member

The Board discussed appointing a third representative to the ACT 170 Merger Committee, which brings together South Burlington, Burlington, and Winooski to explore potential school district consolidation under Vermont state law. Based on student enrollment, South Burlington is allocated three representatives. The committee's first meeting is scheduled for October 20, although the state facilitator has asked districts to initially send only one representative while the process gets underway.

Michelle Boyer was proposed as the third member alongside Seamus Abshere and Dan Boyer, the two previously nominated Board members. Seamus Abshere called for a motion to nominate Michelle Boyer as the third board member for the committee. Jennifer Lawrence moved and Emilee Hoffman seconded the motion. All were in favor; motion passed unanimously.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to nominate Elissa Galvez as an alternate member. Tom Chittenden moved and Michelle Boyer seconded the motion. All were in favor and the motion passed.

### 2.3 Treatment of Community

The Board postponed it to October 21, deciding the Superintendent should prepare it rather than the Board. This aligns with the new Ends Policy, which requires the Superintendent to gather feedback from a representative sample of community members. Since the policy was only recently implemented, the first report is not expected to include results from this new requirement.

## SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT

Joe Clark provided a brief update on the following topics:

**South Point Relocation and Program Expansion:** The South Point move has been completed, providing a new space designed to better meet students' learning and therapeutic needs. The program has expanded to include five middle school students alongside ten high school students, with additional referrals underway. The new location across from the high school also creates opportunities for stronger connections between middle and high school programs.

**District Strategic Plan:** The district's strategic planning process is moving forward with an inclusive committee involving staff, families, students, and community members, supported by a smaller steering committee. Meetings are planned for October, November, and December to assess current district needs, gather community feedback, and to develop a strategic plan to guide the district over the next several years. Community members and students are encouraged to volunteer and participate.

**Fiscal Year 2028 Budget:** The district is taking a new, district-wide approach to budgeting by evaluating staffing based on enrollment, class sizes, student needs, and educational programming rather than automatically carrying forward previous budgets. The review will examine staffing equity across elementary schools, scheduling and course offerings at the middle and high school levels, and opportunities to coordinate purchasing and reduce inefficiencies. Joe Clark emphasized that the budget process is not solely about cutting costs but about directing resources where they will have the greatest impact on students. Potential areas for expanded programming include music, career and technical education, and American Sign Language. He discussed consolidating purchasing of furniture, supplies, and equipment to reduce duplication, improve efficiency, and to use district resources more cost-effectively. The Board will receive further information and budget recommendations over the coming months. He asked the Board to allow the leadership team to present its proposed staffing changes and program priorities before setting the FY28 budget target. The Board will ultimately determine the budget amount presented to voters, and the district will work within that approved limit.

There were no additional comments.

Seamus Abshere asked if there were any questions about the items on the Consent Agenda. Michelle Boyer questioned whether purchasing a truck for snow removal and salting could be avoided through shared services with the city or neighboring school districts. Jean-Marie Clark explained that the district is bringing more snow removal work in-house to reduce contractor costs, requiring updated equipment that typically needs replacement every five years due to salt damage. Although some services were already shared with the city, scheduling and equipment limitations make broader partnerships challenging, but the Board acknowledged that exploring collaboration and joint purchasing with Burlington and Winooski could create future cost savings.

There was some discussion about South Point and all of the work that has been done. Jean-Marie Clark praised the new South Point space, highlighting Katie Cunningham, the program director, for her creative thinking, flexibility, and significant contributions to the space's design and relocation. Despite last-minute challenges and delays in preparing the space before the school year began, her planning helped make the transition as smooth as possible. The Board also agreed to arrange a tour of the new facility before an upcoming meeting.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to approve the bid for the Ford F550 Super Duty campus salting vehicle. Michelle Boyer moved and Elissa Galvez seconded the motion. All were in favor; motion passed.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to approve the AP voucher checks. Tom Chittenden moved and Elissa Galvez seconded the motion. All were in favor; motion passed.

Seamus Abshere asked if there were any objections to the Consent Agenda. Hearing none, the agenda passed by consent.

## AGENDA FOR NEXT MEETING

The following items were added to the October 21 agenda:

- Monthly 2.4 Financial Condition and Activities Review (*Discussion Item*)
- Policy F4 Investigation and Response to Harassment, Hazing, and Bullying of Students (*Discussion Item*) (**Second Reading**)
- Policy D9 Electronic Communications Between Employees and Students (*Discussion Item*) (**Second Reading**)
- Monitoring Report 2.3 Treatment of Community (*Action Item*)
- Updates for The Other Paper

Seamus Abshere asked that any additional topics for the Superintendent's Report be sent to him with time for Joe Clark to prepare.

Michelle Boyer asked about having our representatives come to a meeting post election. There was additional discussion about the NESDEC best use study and whether it should be a separate agenda item to discuss. Seamus Abshere invited any additional items of importance to the agenda, should a Board member want to discuss them in more depth.

## ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, Seamus Abshere called for a motion to adjourn. Emilee Hoffman moved and Tom Chittenden seconded. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting adjourned at 7:35 p.m.
